Dinner options

Price guide is a rough relative scale: $ casual · $$ mid-range · $$$ upscale · $$$$ priciest.

  • Merriman's ($$$) (~5 min from Koloa Landing). Farm-to-table Hawaii Regional Cuisine, the fancy-night pick, dinner 5–8pm with a keiki menu and a GF menu whose staff celiac diners praise for knowing cross-contamination protocol.
  • RumFire Poipu Beach ($$) (~5 min from Koloa Landing). Oceanfront Hawaiian seafood with sunset views and GF-marked dishes like misoyaki butterfish, open Thu–Sun 5–9pm — OpenTable lists it as permanently closed while its own site and recent reviews show it operating, so confirm before going.
  • Brennecke's Beach Broiler ($$) (~5 min from Koloa Landing). Casual open-air ocean-view grill with fresh seafood, steak, salads and a GF-options menu, plus a 3–5pm happy hour and live music Thu–Sat.
  • Duke's Kauai ($$) (~25 min from Koloa Landing). Classic oceanfront Hawaiian grill with live music daily, a keiki menu, GF options, and the famous Hula Pie — big, family-friendly, worth the drive to Lihue.
  • Hukilau Lanai ($$) (~40 min from Koloa Landing). Open-air lanai serving fresh local fish nightly with live music and thoughtful allergy accommodation — the east-side standout, open Mon–Sat 5–9pm.
  • Eating House 1849 ($$$) (~5 min from Koloa Landing). Roy Yamaguchi's Hawaii Regional Cuisine spot in the Shops at Kukui'ula with a plantation-house feel, GF options, and a kids' menu — a polished night out close to the resort.
  • Holo Holo ($$) — at the resort. The resort's own restaurant, steps from the villas, with island dishes and GF options — the easiest table for a big group night.
  • Red Salt ($$$$) — the priciest option; consider for the adults' night only (~5 min from Koloa Landing). Fine-dining Hawaii Regional Cuisine at Ko'a Kea Resort with a GF-aware kitchen.
  • Casa Kalaheo (~15 min from Koloa Landing). Casual Mexican in Kalaheo, no reservations — Jeannie's suggestion for Sun Dec 27 dinner; the whole group could go, or a few order takeout and bring it back. GF items listed (quesadillas, enchiladas, tacos); confirm with staff on the day.

Lunch options

  • Kauai Poke Co. (top pick) (~7 min from Koloa Landing). Fresh ahi poke bowls at the Poipu Bay Golf Course clubhouse — the Plantation bowl is the house favorite; tamari shoyu option for gluten free. Open daily 10am–3pm.
  • Cabana Bar & Grill (Jeannie's pick) (~5 min from Koloa Landing). Relaxed poolside bar and grill at 2290 Poipu Rd, inside the Poipu Beach Athletic Club, 11am–8pm daily — fish tacos, burgers, salads, kids' menu, 3–5pm happy hour, with GF options praised by celiac diners.
  • Da Crack Mexican Grinds (~5 min from Koloa Landing). Walk-up taco window at Kukui'ula Market, 11am–8pm daily — ahi fish tacos and rice bowls (corn tortillas and rice bowls are the GF route); takeout only, so plan to eat at the villa or beach.
  • Koloa Fish Market (~8 min from Koloa Landing). Family-owned takeout fish market with some of the island's best poke (all but two varieties GF) and rice-based plate lunches — open Mon–Wed/Fri/Sat 10am–3pm, closed Sun and Thu.
  • Chicken in a Barrel BBQ (~30 min from Koloa Landing). Barrel-smoked BBQ on the drive back from Waimea Canyon — grilled chicken, pulled pork, ribs and rice widely reported GF (skip fried items, chili disputed — confirm with staff).
  • Caba. Sandwich shop in Hanapepe, 3840 Hanapepe Rd — Jeannie's pick for sandwiches after the Dec 28 charter; well-reviewed, with GF bread/buns. On the drive back from Kekaha/Waimea toward Poipu, so it fits as a post-charter stop.
  • Living Foods Market & Cafe (~5 min from Koloa Landing). Open-air cafe and market at the Shops at Kukui'ula, 7am–9pm daily, with a GF menu (GF bread for smash burgers, salads, poke bowls) and an attached market — the sit-down, group-friendly lunch closest to the resort.
  • Kalaheo Cafe (~20 min from Koloa Landing). Small-town cafe in Kalaheo on the way to Waimea Canyon — already the group's breakfast stop for the canyon day — serving local plates with GF-friendly options.

Na Pali Coast Private Charter CONFIRMED — Dec 28

Na Pali Experience · Mon Dec 28, 2026 · 7:30 AM – 12:00 PM
Check-in 7:00 AM · Kikiaola Small Boat Harbor, Kekaha, Kauai, HI 96752 · Booking #367422570 · Party of 15

  • Changes: Cancel/reschedule up to 48 hrs prior
  • Waivers: Required for all, including minors — do before the day
  • Minimum age: 4
  • Parking: $20 per car at the harbor
  • Prep: No coffee beforehand; pack light

Lunch after docking: Chicken in a Barrel BBQ, Waimea (9400 Kaumualii Hwy) — BBQ plates (grilled chicken, pulled pork, ribs) and rice reported gluten free; skip fried items (no dedicated fryer), the chili is disputed, so confirm with staff on the day.

Departure point — confirm before Dec 28: DLNR's facility-notices page (last updated Oct 5, 2026) still lists Kikiaola Small Boat Harbor as closed until further notice after Hurricane Lowell damage, while the operator still lists Kikiaola departures — confirm the departure point with Na Pali Experience ahead of the day.

Surf Lessons CONFIRMED — Dec 29

Kauai Surf School · Tue Dec 29, 2026 · Poipu Beach
12 people, three reservations · Kiahuna Plantation, Poipu (~5 min from Koloa Landing)

  • 10:00–11:30 AM — the four boys: Dash, Max, Sam, Mason (Booking #392251883, Order #GPQJDJ)
  • 12:00–1:30 PM — the five girls: Natalie, Rory, Phoebe, Madeline (Booking #392252394, Order #GPQJHY)

Meet: Kauai Surf School Beach Activity Hut, Kiahuna Plantation Resort, Poipu Road, Poipu, HI 96756 — check in at the hut on the grass above Kiahuna Beach at least 15 minutes early; public parking at the end of Poipu Beach Road / Hoonani Road across from the Sheraton, follow Beach Access signs into Kiahuna Plantation. Bring a towel and reef-safe sunscreen, swimwear on; rash-guards provided. Online waivers required for all 12 before arrival. Cancel at least 24 hours before for a full refund or credit; full refund or credit if the operator cancels for hazardous weather.

Poipu Beach itself: The lessons are right on Poipu Beach — lifeguarded, with a protected lagoon. Turtles bask on the sand in the afternoons and evenings, and monk seals sometimes haul out there to rest. The south shore is the calm, swimmable side of the island in December.

Hikes MAYBE

Grouped by area. Drive times are typical driving times from Koloa Landing.

North Shore / Na Pali

  • Kalalau Trail to Hanakāpīʻai Beach (~1 hr 40 min from Koloa Landing). 4 miles round trip, 3–4 hours, steep and muddy with one stream crossing, ending at a remote beach under the Na Pali cliffs. Day hiking to Hanakāpīʻai is open, but Hāʻena State Park entry is reservation-only through gohaena.com, released 30 days out, and sells out fast. December is the wet season — check for flash-flood closures the morning of, and don't plan on swimming at the beach. Natural fit for the possible Thu Dec 31 North Shore day; reservations for Dec 31 open Dec 1.

Waimea Canyon / Koke'e

  • Canyon Trail to Waipo'o Falls (~1 hr 10 min from Koloa Landing). About 3–4 miles round trip, ~2 hours, moderate, to the top of the 800-foot falls. Kid-friendly for the older kids (8+), muddy even on dry days; start by 8am before clouds build. The hike for the Wed Dec 30 Waimea day.
  • Nu'alolo Trail (~1 hr 10 min from Koloa Landing). 7.5 miles round trip, 4–6 hours, hard, dropping from 3,800 feet to Lolo Vista, a cliff-top view over the Na Pali coast. Out-and-back only — the old loop through Awa'awapuhi is not possible right now. Best for the teens and adults.
  • Pihea Trail / Pihea Vista (~1 hr 25 min from Koloa Landing). Short version to Pihea Vista: about 2.3 miles round trip, ~1 hour, easy to moderate, with Kalalau Valley views nearly as good as the Kalalau Trail for a fraction of the effort. Full trail runs 3.8 miles one way into the Alaka'i Swamp boardwalk. Go 8–11am for the best chance of clear views; expect deep mud.
  • Iliau Nature Loop (add-on) — 0.3-mile easy loop on the canyon rim past the rare iliau plant; a 10-minute add-on on the Waimea day, not a hike on its own.

Not an option right now: Awa'awapuhi Trail — open only to its first mile, so its cliff viewpoint isn't reachable.

South Shore / Poipu

  • Maha'ulepu Heritage Trail (~7 min from Koloa Landing). About 4 miles round trip, 1.5–2.5 hours, easy to moderate along limestone sea cliffs from Shipwreck Beach. Free, no permit. Winter bonus: whales offshore. Nearby Makauwahi Cave Reserve is closed.

Also closed right now: Sleeping Giant and Kuilau Ridge Trail (east side, near Wailua).

Allerton Garden MAYBE

Guided walking tour of the garden (~8 min from Koloa Landing), about 2.5 hours, about $63.60 per person. Guided tours only — wear closed-toe shoes. Check in at the South Shore Visitors Center, across from Spouting Horn.

Spouting Horn MAYBE

A blowhole on the rocky shore at Lawai that shoots seawater skyward with each wave — right across the street from the Allerton Garden check-in (South Shore Visitors Center), so it pairs naturally with an Allerton visit. Free roadside stop, just a few minutes; best at high tide and with a south swell. ~8 min from Koloa Landing.

North Shore Lighthouse (Kilauea Point) MAYBE

Possible Thu Dec 31 North Shore day (morning, weather and energy permitting). Kilauea Point (~1 hr 10 min from Koloa Landing) is open Wed–Sat, 10 AM–4 PM only — closed Sun/Mon and federal holidays (closed Jan 1). Timed-entry reservations are required via Recreation.gov: $10 per adult 16+ plus a $1 booking fee ($11 total), under 16 free — 7 paying people for this crew = $77. Lighthouse interior tours are suspended. Pair it with a Hanalei Bay stop (~1 hr 20 min from Koloa Landing) — scenery, pier and town; winter surf makes it a no-swim beach — plus lunch in Kilauea/Hanalei town.

Kayaking (Wailua River) MAYBE

Wailua River kayak tours currently run paddle-only, Mon–Fri. The Secret Falls (Uluwehi Falls) trail is still closed until further notice, with no reopening date, so there's no hike to the falls. $5 per person Wailua Marina entry fee; age 4+. A weekly status check is running.
